title: Invariant affine neighbourhoods descend along integral orbit covers
statement: Let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Assume $s,t$ are integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $a:T\to U$ be integral and assume every $R$-orbit meets $a(T)$, where the $R$-orbit of $u\in U$ is the set $t(s^{-1}(\{u\}))$ of targets of points $r\in R$ with $s(r)=u$. For a morphism $a:T\to U$, the restricted groupoid has object scheme $T$ and arrow scheme $T\times_{a,U,s}R\times_{t,U,a}T$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with induced source, target and groupoid operations. If $x\in T$ lies in an affine open $V\subseteq T$ with $s_T^{-1}(V)=t_T^{-1}(V)$ as open subschemes, then $a(x)$ lies in an affine open $W\subseteq U$ with $s^{-1}(W)=t^{-1}(W)$.

proof.text: First record the point-lifting consequence of the cited statements. Given scheme points $y,z$ with the same image $b$, the ring $\kappa(y)\otimes_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(z)$ is nontrivial by the field-tensor lemma, so it has a maximal prime ideal by the maximal-ideal lemma. The fibre-product-points lemma therefore supplies a point of the fibre product projecting to exactly $y,z$. We use this consequence repeatedly, including for iterated fibre products.

source.place: Tag 0ABE, lemma-find-affine-integral, proof; pointwise lifting needed for the set-theoretic assertions labelled details omitted; auxiliary Tag 01JT (schemes.tex, lemma-points-fibre-product).

proof.text: Write $u\sim v$ when some $r\in R$ has $s(r)=u,t(r)=v$. This is an equivalence relation: $e$ gives reflexivity, $i$ symmetry, and for arrows from $u$ to $v$ and from $v$ to $w$, Step 1 lifts their two points to the composition fibre product, where $c$ gives an arrow from $u$ to $w$. Similarly, $y\sim_T z$ holds exactly when $a(y)\sim a(z)$: projection gives one implication; for the other, lift the witnessing arrow together with $y,z$ successively by Step 1 to $T\times_{a,U,s}R\times_{t,U,a}T$. Thus the assumed equality of inverse images of $V$ says that $V$ contains every $\sim_T$-equivalence class which meets it.

source.place: Tag 0ABE, lemma-find-affine-integral, proof; details omitted: groupoid laws and the restricted groupoid; composition and two successive point lifts.

proof.text: Put $P=T\times_{a,U,t}R$, with $p:P\to T$, $q:P\to R$, and $h=s\circ q:P\to U$. The map $p$ is the base change of the integral map $t$ and $q$ is the base change of the integral map $a$. Hence $p,q$ are integral, and composition with the integral map $s$ makes $h$ integral. Set $\widetilde V=p^{-1}(V)$. Integral morphisms are affine by definition, so the affine-open inverse-image clause applied to $p$ shows that $\widetilde V$ is affine.

source.place: Tag 0ABE, lemma-find-affine-integral, proof; first three sentences: construction of tilde R and integrality of the projections and h.

proof.text: Set $W=h(\widetilde V)\subseteq|U|$. By Step 1, $u\in W$ is equivalent to $u\sim a(v)$ for some $v\in V$. Consequently $W$ is a union of $R$-orbits by Step 2. We prove $h^{-1}(W)=\widetilde V$. The inclusion from right to left is the definition of $W$. If $z\in P$ and $h(z)\in W$, choose $v\in V$ with $h(z)\sim a(v)$. The arrow $q(z)$ gives $h(z)\sim a(p(z))$, hence $a(p(z))\sim a(v)$. Step 2 gives $p(z)\sim_T v$, so invariance of $V$ implies $p(z)\in V$, or $z\in\widetilde V$. Also $a(x)\in W$ since $x\in V$ and $a(x)\sim a(x)$.

source.place: Tag 0ABE, lemma-find-affine-integral, proof; details omitted: W is invariant and tilde W is the full inverse image of W; membership of the requested point.

proof.text: The map $h$ is surjective: for any $u\in U$, choose $y\in T$ with $a(y)$ in the orbit $t(s^{-1}(\{u\}))$. By definition of the orbit there is an arrow with source $u$ and target $a(y)$; Step 1 lifts it and $y$ to $P$. Its image under $h$ is $u$. Since $h$ is integral, it is universally closed by the cited characterization, hence closed by the definition, using the identity base change. Step 4 and surjectivity give $U\setminus W=h(P\setminus\widetilde V)$. The latter is closed because $\widetilde V$ is open and $h$ is closed. Therefore $W$ is open; give it its open subscheme structure.

source.place: Tag 0ABE, lemma-find-affine-integral, proof; last three sentences: orbit-surjectivity, closedness of integral morphisms (Tag 01WM), and quotient-topology argument, here written via complements.

proof.text: The inverse image of the open subscheme $W$ under $h$ is exactly $\widetilde V$ by Step 4. Thus $\widetilde V\to W$ is the base change of $h$ along $W\hookrightarrow U$, and is integral and surjective. Its source is affine by Step 3, so the cited affine-target theorem implies that $W$ is affine. Since $W$ is a union of the equivalence classes of Step 2, for every $r\in R$ one has $s(r)\in W$ if and only if $t(r)\in W$. The inverse-image open subschemes therefore agree: $s^{-1}(W)=t^{-1}(W)$. Together with $a(x)\in W$ from Step 4 this is the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0ABE, lemma-find-affine-integral, proof; middle of proof: integral-surjective affine descent, Tag 05YU (limits.tex, proposition-affine), and final invariant neighbourhood.
